title: Classes, ids and attributes
summary: Label elements with class, id and data-* attributes, set the page language, and use div and span.

options: Many elements may share one id
An id must be unique on the page
An id can only be a number
An id is shown to visitors
quiz.explain: An id identifies one element, so reusing it breaks links and scripts. Use `class` for groups.

quiz.q: Store a price on the element with a custom data attribute.
quiz.explain: Custom attributes must start with `data-`, for example `data-price`.

quiz.q: Which element is right for highlighting two words **inside** a sentence?
quiz.explain: `span` is inline, so it stays within the line. `div` and `p` start on a new line.

quiz.q: Click the line that breaks the rule about ids.
quiz.explain: The id `intro` is used twice. Change one to a class, or give it a different id.

exercise.task:
Mark up the shop page in `index.html`.

- Add `lang="en"` to the `<html>` element.
- Give the intro paragraph `id="intro"`.
- Make two `<div>` elements with `class="card"`, each with a `data-price` attribute.
- Make the second card also have the class `featured`.
- In the intro paragraph wrap the word `fresh` in `<span class="highlight">`.
hints: Edit the starter: change the html tag, then add the id and the span in the paragraph, then add the two divs.
A second class is added with a space: class="card featured". data-price needs a value like "499".

...

Everything is fresh today.
